node: HVDC transformer winding components, continuously transposed conductors, and qualified grid-OEM inputs
summary: Layer 1B expansion found very limited clean US-listed exposure to continuously transposed conductor or paper-insulated transformer winding inputs. The most direct public-market anchors are large OEM/grid-equipment names that consume or integrate these inputs, while the underfollowed lane is more likely to sit in adjacent qualified utility hardware and component suppliers rather than pure CTC. KSH International remains the clearest seed for the India HVDC/CTC chokepoint, but it is not US-listed. For US-listed research, PLPC is the most plausible underfollowed second-order candidate because utility-specified transmission hardware can share the same approval/specification-lock characteristics, although it is not a transformer-winding supplier. Direct CTC exposure through US-listed names remains a coverage gap requiring verification via OEM approved-vendor lists, transformer bill-of-material disclosures, and supplier certifications.
